journey.title: Escape closes only the innermost open submenu
journey.goal: Escape in the Facts submenu returns to Facts while the About submenu stays open

functionalJourney.title: Open nested submenus with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: About and Facts submenus open on click

guards.title: Escape in a first-level submenu returns to the menubar
guards.goal: Escape in the About submenu closes it and focuses About

plan.root_cause: Escape key handling in submenus incorrectly closes all submenus via rootMenu.closeChildren() instead of closing only the current submenu.
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the Escape case in the submenu keyup handler to close the current submenu using its controller and focus the controller's toggle element.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will close only the innermost open submenu and return focus to its parent menu item, keeping parent submenus open as expected.
functional_risks: If a submenu somehow lacks a controller, the close operation will be skipped (no error).
Focusing the toggle element may not scroll into view if the container overflows, but this matches the original behavior for menu items.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape on #history results in focus on #facts, aria-expanded facts=false, aria-expanded about=true.
Verify that Escape on a top-level menubar item still closes the menubar and focuses the controller.
Verify that Escape on a submenu item that has its own submenu (e.g., #overview if it had a submenu) correctly closes that submenu and focuses the parent item.

plan.root_cause: Escape key handling in submenus incorrectly calls rootMenu.closeChildren() and rootMenu.focusCurrentChild(), which closes all submenus and returns focus to the menubar. Submenus do not have a direct controller reference in elements.controller; the toggle belongs to the parent menu's submenuToggles array at the same index as the submenu in the parent's dom.submenus array.
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the Escape case in the submenu keyup handler to find the parent menu's toggle for this submenu, close that toggle, and focus the toggle element.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will close only the innermost open submenu and return focus to its parent menu item, keeping parent submenus open as expected.
functional_risks: If a submenu somehow lacks a corresponding toggle in the parent menu, the close operation will be skipped (no error).
Focusing the toggle element may not scroll into view if the container overflows, but this matches the original behavior for menu items.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape on #history results in focus on #facts, aria-expanded facts=false, aria-expanded about=true.
Verify that Escape on a top-level menubar item still closes the menubar and focuses the controller.
Verify that Escape on a submenu item that has its own submenu (e.g., #overview if it had a submenu) correctly closes that submenu and focuses the parent item.
